dataModelChanges.details: New host-owned plain data/types, not model output. Snapshot: provider claude|codex; issues[{code,field,correction,message?,occurrences}]; optional terminal{reason,exitCode?,message?}; optional lastRejectedFeedback{preview,truncated}. ReviewOutputFailureError extends Error and carries this bounded snapshot across provider failures. Errors derive from JSON parser, existing AJV keyword/path details, native terminal envelopes or known host validation errors only. Static correction examples: missing required findings -> MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD / findings / 'Return findings as a top-level JSON array.'; invalid JSON -> INVALID_JSON / '/' / 'Return one valid JSON object.' Do not invent FIELD_EMBEDDED_IN_SUMMARY from text or parse markup into missing fields. Capture only whitelisted output/error fields, never reasoning/prompts/raw tool results.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: At most 8 distinct issues per snapshot; code <=64 chars; field/correction <=256 UTF-8 bytes each; message <=1024 UTF-8 bytes; preview <=8192 UTF-8 bytes. Count repeated issues rather than append. Current-attempt diagnostic total <=32 KiB. Drop preview then long message first and mark truncation. Preserve existing 4 MiB whole-checkpoint bound; if compact codes cannot fit, surface save failure rather than falsely acknowledge or silently lose them.

dataModelChanges.details: Optional host-owned array of {phase:'attribution'|'assessment',taskId?:string,diagnostic:ReviewDiagnosticSnapshot}. Relationship: one attempt owns zero or more entries; assessment entries each belong to exactly one selected task; one attribution entry omits taskId and applies to the selected task set. Replace latest current-execution snapshot using existing atomic serial writer and execution fences. Do not multiply shared attribution evidence per task. TaskReviewResult/native schema remains unchanged. Old checkpoints/CRs need no rewrite or backfill. This field remains in existing temporary checkpoint, cleaned by normal story BUILD approval ownership; no new recovery file/cleanup mechanism.

Derived explicit input property {previousRoundFeedback:[{attempt,taskId,phase,errors:[{code,field,correction}]}],previousRoundFeedbackTruncated?:true}. Not submitter input. For each task/phase inspect the latest earlier same-reviewer attempt only; include supported diagnostics if that task/phase remains unresolved. A newer successful result suppresses older errors. Assignment prompt includes its task; attribution includes applicable selected tasks/shared phase. Missing/foreign/history-without-diagnostics gives []. At most 8 errors per task and 4 KiB UTF-8 across the whole projected feedback including truncation marker. Stable deduplication; no schema repetition or native/candidate snippets. Omit raw failureDiagnostics from all ordinary embedded history so another prompt section cannot reintroduce verbose evidence. Complete checkpoint remains available through existing read tools if needed.

migration.stateBefore: s1 grounded parser drops invalid-candidate details and generic activity exit loses native errors; checkpoints have no explicit error feedback.
migration.stateAfter: Native adapters/hosts persist bounded host-owned evidence and next-attempt inputs receive concise previousRoundFeedback; strict model results/finality and all earlier attempts stay unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add optional stored diagnostic/plain issue contracts while keeping native model result schemas unchanged; verify old fixtures.
Connect both native adapters and host routes through diagnostic sink/existing activity exchange with strict execution fencing.
Project concise feedback in attribution and assessment and omit raw diagnostic history from inline context.
Deploy with normal daemon restart after BUILD approval. Do not backfill old histories or automatically start S2 review.

migration.backwardCompat: New optional checkpoint fields preserve existing old data in new readers; model/submitter schemas unchanged. Updated controller native integration wires optional onDiagnostic for parity. Old strict binaries may reject new diagnostic checkpoints; do not strip/rewrite history to downgrade active runs. No legacy engine, fallback flag or new persistence mechanism.
